one_line: Semantic debugger for the agentic web.
what_it_does: Tests WebMCP applications against declared human intent, guardrails, effects, and safety boundaries, producing explainable parity traces and findings.
leverage_rationale: Structured WebMCP inspection and parity auditing are central to the product; general UI-driving agents could not as reliably preserve provenance and compare semantic intent with technical effects.
leverage_evidence: About text describes five page-defined WebMCP meta-tools including run_parity_audit and trace_goal.
Controlled broken/fixed paths distinguish an HTTP-successful but unsafe mutation from a read-only safe path.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent testing workflow and a concrete broken/fixed demonstration, but the submitted packet has no video transcript and image inspection was unavailable, limiting end-to-end confirmation.
execution_evidence: About text specifies contract inputs, execution adapter provenance, X-Ray trace, findings, recommendations, and PASS/WARN/FAIL statuses.
Facts report a live demo and public repository.
impact_rationale: Agentic-web developers have a specific safety and semantic-regression problem, and the proposed audit layer directly addresses failures that ordinary HTTP/tool success checks miss.
impact_evidence: About text identifies user-intent violations and skipped review boundaries as the target problem.
Broken Subly Playground scenario demonstrates a realistic subscription/charge safety failure.
creativity_rationale: The semantic-parity framing is a fresh and memorable extension beyond ordinary WebMCP demos, with a focused testing model rather than a generic agent wrapper.
creativity_evidence: Separates Human Surface intent, Agent Surface tools, effects, and safety boundaries.
Uses explainable semantic X-Ray traces and parity statuses.
usability_note: The contract-and-trace workflow appears useful for developers, though evidence of the live interaction is limited.
red_flags: No submitted video; visual evidence could not be independently checked.
advance_reason: Strong, differentiated WebMCP-native developer problem with credible impact; advance despite limited visual verification.

one_line: A read-only, evidence-aware architecture map shared by people and agents.
what_it_does: Maps project interfaces, routes, APIs, capabilities, handlers, data, audit contracts, and runtime evidence while exposing bypasses and uncertainty.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools operate on the same semantic graph as the visual explorer, enabling precise path tracing and fail-closed findings that would be difficult to reproduce through UI scraping.
leverage_evidence: Five WebMCP tools inspect overview, focus entities, trace paths, list findings, and compare layers.
Unknown or fuzzy requests fail closed without changing selection.
execution_rationale: The described read-only explorer has a coherent scope and explicit uncertainty states, but no video transcript and unavailable image review reduce confidence in completeness.
execution_evidence: About text defines graph entities, evidence states, bypass visualization, and read-only boundaries.
Facts report a live demo and public repository.
impact_rationale: Architecture drift, missing controls, and bypasses are real problems for teams maintaining complex software; a shared evidence-aware map can improve review and agent context.
impact_evidence: About text names drift between screens, permissions, services, data, and audit rules.
Explicit BYPASS finding exposes a direct UI-to-handler path.
creativity_rationale: The shared graph plus uncertainty-preserving architecture exploration is a fresh synthesis, though architecture mapping is an established category.
creativity_evidence: Combines human visual exploration with agent access to identical semantic entities.
Makes Needs Proof, Blind Spot, and Review states first-class.
usability_note: Read-only and fail-closed behavior supports safe exploration; density of the graph may create onboarding burden.
red_flags: No submitted video; visual claims not independently checked.
standouts: BYPASS and uncertainty states make architectural risk legible.
advance_reason: Clear developer audience and meaningful WebMCP leverage with a differentiated evidence model.

leverage_rationale: The packet describes a useful browser-local deterministic workflow, but WebMCP-specific leverage is not evidenced; ordinary UI interaction appears able to achieve the same outcome.
leverage_evidence: About text emphasizes local deterministic layout and export rather than an agent-centered shared state.

execution_rationale: The problem and solution are coherent, but there is no submitted video and the packet does not provide enough checked visual evidence for end-to-end execution credit.

impact_evidence: About text identifies manual layout friction, dimension inaccuracies, privacy risks, and paper waste.

one_line: A shared command room for rehearsing changing fire-safety conditions with human approval.
what_it_does: Lets a facilitator and agent rehearse a building scenario, inspect shared 2D/3D state, assign assistance, handle blocked routes, and produce a human-approved after-action report.
leverage_rationale: The agent and facilitator share live structured floor-plan, roster, assignment, path, and approval state; this collaboration is substantially more reliable than generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text describes shared live floor plan and synchronized 2D, 3D, profile, roster, and tool readback.
Human-gated confirmation separates preparation from assignment and preserves final report approval.
execution_rationale: The packet lays out a detailed, coherent central rehearsal loop with state synchronization and safety boundaries; visual completion remains unverified.
execution_evidence: Try-working-loop instructions cover scenario start/resume, 3D inspection, tool readback, assignment confirmation, route changes, responsibility gaps, and report draft.
Facts report a live demo and public repository.
impact_rationale: Fire-safety managers and exercise teams have a concrete training and coordination need, and rehearsal of changing conditions can produce meaningful preparedness value.
impact_evidence: About text targets building Fire Safety Managers and exercise teams.
Scenario includes unavailable stairs, assisted occupants, responsibility gaps, and after-action review.
creativity_rationale: A human-agent tabletop fire-drill workspace with synchronized 2D/3D state and explicit approval boundaries is memorable and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Combines spatial rehearsal, agent queries, structured assignments, and after-action learning.
Explicitly frames itself as fictional training rather than live emergency software.
usability_note: Guided scenario controls and visible confirmation boundaries suggest strong usability for facilitated exercises.
red_flags: No submitted video; image evidence could not be independently checked.
standouts: Synchronized spatial views and human approval at consequential boundaries.
advance_reason: High WebMCP leverage, clear audience value, and unusually coherent ambitious workflow.

one_line: An owner-controlled WebMCP read layer for existing websites.
what_it_does: Exposes typed, bounded search, content, listing, and sitemap tools with owner governance, canonical URLs, Markdown, and server-enforced human-only boundaries.
leverage_rationale: The owner-selected, revocable, same-origin typed surface materially improves reliable agent access to site content and governance over what agents may do.
leverage_evidence: About text describes document.modelContext.registerTool and bounded same-origin MCP endpoint.
Server refuses the write-shaped expert-call tool as human_only before storage or email; product-level purchase policies are explicit.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent reusable contract, a live flagship, eleven deployed stacks, and explicit policy behavior; no video means visual end-to-end confidence is limited.
execution_evidence: Four core read-only tools are shared across integrations.
Facts report live demo and public repository; about text names deployed flagship and protocol.
impact_rationale: Website owners and agents need authoritative, governed access without DOM reverse engineering; the bounded contract addresses both reliability and safety.
impact_evidence: About text identifies current browser-agent failures in authority discovery and permission understanding.
Eleven stacks and explicit per-product purchase policies show a practical deployment target.
creativity_rationale: A reusable owner-controlled contract layer with governed extensions is a strong systems idea, though typed website read layers have adjacent precedents.
creativity_evidence: Capabilities live with pages and can be revoked without changing human-facing pages.
Policy metadata distinguishes agent-allowed purchases from human-only actions.
usability_note: Read-only canonical Markdown and explicit governance should make agent/site collaboration predictable.
red_flags: No submitted video; deployment claims are packet claims rather than observed here.
standouts: Owner governance and server-enforced human-only boundary.
advance_reason: Strong practical WebMCP infrastructure with credible deployment and governance evidence.

one_line: A WebMCP-native marketplace where people and outside agents share a durable deal workspace.
what_it_does: Supports marketplace browsing, boards, alerts, research notebooks, comparisons, offers, trades, and human approvals through a shared persistent canvas.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central: outside agents re-discover authenticated capabilities, manipulate durable shared canvas state, preserve evidence, and stop at human verification boundaries—well beyond UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes signed-out setup tools, post-login capability rediscovery, 121 structured tools, and persistent human-agent state.
Publishing, alerts, seller contact, offers, and trade advancement require human approval and outcomes are recorded.
execution_rationale: The 165-second video transcript and detailed product description cover a broad coherent workflow from discovery through research and approval, with explicit state and control boundaries.
execution_evidence: Facts report video=True, 165 seconds, live demo, public repository.
Transcript describes browsing, boards, cited research, cost calculations, offer plans, undo history, and multi-party trade rooms.
impact_rationale: Collectors and buyers have a real discovery, comparison, research, and negotiation coordination problem; the shared workspace directly reduces scattered evidence and decision friction.
impact_evidence: About text names old cars, boats, campers, motorcycles, and machinery buyers as the audience.
Transcript shows compound search, comparable sales, inspection risks, acquisition-cost calculations, and multi-party trades.
creativity_rationale: The outside-agent marketplace premise, canvas-first collaboration, focused capability packs, and durable evidence-to-decision workflow are highly original and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Marketplace contains no embedded LLM while remaining natively legible to trusted outside agents.
Shared canvas carries findings, notes, decisions, alerts, conversations, offers, and trade rooms.
usability_note: Canvas-first progressive enhancement and explicit approval boundaries are strong, though the breadth of capabilities may be demanding.
red_flags: Requires sign-in for the full workspace.
standouts: Persistent shared canvas and unusually complete human-agent commerce lifecycle.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage with strong video-backed execution, audience value, and ambition.

one_line: A WebMCP media bin that builds scene-ordered video assets on a live canvas.

leverage_rationale: The agent populates and edits a shared visible board while the human iterates visually; structured per-scene tools and in-place writes are materially better than generic UI driving.

impact_rationale: Video creators routinely face fragmented asset sourcing, naming, and scene organization; a visual iterative media bin directly addresses that workflow.
impact_evidence: About text identifies juggling image, stock, audio, TTS, music, and video-reference tabs.

creativity_rationale: Reframing ChatGPT as operator of a live visual canvas, with surgical asset replacement and multi-modal scene assembly, is a fresh and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: No in-app chat; human watches while outside agent fills the board.
Progressive enhancement preserves plain buttons without an agent.
usability_note: Scene-oriented board and surgical replacement should support iterative creative direction; asset breadth may add complexity.
red_flags: No transcript; frame evidence could not be independently checked.
standouts: Strong shared visual-canvas model for agent-assisted creative curation.
advance_reason: Clear creator pain point and meaningful agent/canvas interaction with strong creative ambition.

leverage_rationale: The product depends on durable shared case state, provenance, idempotent lifecycle, and a human trust transition; a chatbot or UI-driving agent would be substantially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: About text says tools update visible source board, diagnostic proposals, evidence graph, and pending state.

execution_rationale: The conceptual workflow and safety boundaries are unusually coherent, but no video or frame sheets were submitted, so execution claims cannot receive high confidence.
execution_evidence: About text defines product identification, source gathering, competing hypotheses, checks, observations, provenance, and stop conditions.
Facts report a live demo and public repository.
impact_rationale: Consumers often need current repair guidance but agents cannot observe physical symptoms; the division of labor is credible and safety-aware for low-risk triage.
impact_evidence: About text names concrete sensory observations unavailable to remote agents.
Recall, battery, smoke, electrical, gas, refrigerant, and pressure hazards stop diagnostics.

creativity_evidence: Competing hypotheses visibly update from confirmed observations.

usability_note: Evidence graph and guided checks can support users, but safety-oriented flows must remain exceptionally clear; implementation is unverified.

standouts: Honest human/agent capability split and hazard-triggered professional-help state.
advance_reason: High impact and WebMCP fit; advance with execution confidence capped because no visual evidence was supplied.

one_line: Structured procedures that people and agents write, run, and improve together.
what_it_does: Stores procedures as checked, conditional steps; runs them with confirmations or blockers; and feeds observed failures back into agent-assisted revisions.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables the agent to read and edit the same structured procedure and live run state while the human confirms checks; this is more reliable and repeatable than editing prose through UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About text says procedures are structured data with instructions, proof checks, and conditions.
Blockers are pinned to failed steps and the agent amends the procedure from the run.
execution_rationale: The write-run-improve loop is coherent and purposefully scoped, but no transcript and unavailable frame inspection limit end-to-end execution confidence.
execution_evidence: About text specifies authoring, conditional execution, confirmations, blocker capture, and post-run amendment.
Facts report a live demo and public repository.
impact_rationale: Teams maintaining operational procedures face real drift and correction problems; capturing blockers at the moment of failure creates direct practical value.
impact_evidence: About text gives onboarding, backup restoration, and credential rotation as concrete procedures.
Identifies the real-world problem that wrong procedures are discovered under time pressure and silently worked around.
creativity_rationale: The closed feedback loop from procedure execution failure to agent-assisted repair is a strong interaction model and a deeper use of WebMCP than a documentation chatbot.
creativity_evidence: Every step has proof expectations and optional branching conditions.
Run-time blocker becomes structured input for improving the originating procedure.
usability_note: Step-level checks and visible agent changes support trust, though procedure editing during operations needs careful UX.
red_flags: No submitted video; visual execution claims could not be independently checked.
standouts: Operational feedback loop that turns blockers into durable procedure improvements.
advance_reason: Clear operational audience, meaningful shared-state leverage, and an original write-run-improve loop.
